decision: umn_ext 'Growing pumpkins and winter squash': "Plant pumpkin and winter squash seeds three-fourths of an inch deep, 24 to 36 inches apart. Use the closer spacing if the variety is a bush type. Spacing between rows should be 5 to 6 feet." -> row-none default, in_row [24,36], rows [60,72] (today [24,48]). DECISION ROW (not a D1 repair: worklist 56 §3). VCE 426-331 Table 5, cited, states 'Squash, winter 2-4 ft 3-10 ft' = today's [24,48] with rows [36,120]. CHOSEN: UMN 'Plant pumpkin and winter squash seeds ... 24 to 36 inches apart ... Spacing between rows should be 5 to 6 feet' -> [24,36]/[60,72], for two reasons: (1) acorn and butternut (same winter-squash group) take UMN in the ruled D1 repairs, so all three winter squash read one page and one figure; (2) the crop's own prose already says 2-3 ft in-row (VCE's 4 ft hi is on no spaghetti prose), and VCE's 3-10 ft row span is too wide to guide a gardener. Alternative (keep VCE [24,48], no move, no edits) is a one-line flip. Restatements: rows '3 to 5 feet' -> '5 to 6 feet'. No hill entry: the only hill figure on its cited pages is UGA C1206, a PUMPKIN page ('Plant pumpkins in hills, with at least 8 feet of space on all sides'), out of scope (worklist 56 §3).

edits.new: Pick a sunny spot with rich, well-drained soil and mix in plenty of compost before planting, since spaghetti squash is a large, hungry plant. Plant it on low hills or mounds, which warm up and drain better. Give it room: space plants about 2 to 3 feet apart in rows 5 to 6 feet apart, since the vines can spread 6 to 8 feet (bush types like Tivoli need less). If your soil is heavy or wet, build the mounds up higher so water drains away from the roots and fruit.
edits.reason: PLA-10 R3: rows follow the authored row_spacing_inches [60,72] (UMN)

edits.new: Prepare a fertile, well-drained bed in full sun, working several inches of compost or rotted manure into the soil before planting, since spaghetti squash is a hungry, long-season plant. Many growers set plants in low hills or mounds about a foot across, which warm faster in spring, drain better, and give the vines a clear starting point. Space generously: roughly 24 to 36 inches between plants in the row with 5 to 6 feet between rows for vining types (closer for bush types like Tivoli), because the vines can run 6 to 8 feet. On heavy or wet ground, build the mounds up for drainage to head off crown and fruit rot.
